subject: Pilot readiness: hosted endpoints, rate ceilings, and VPC decision inputs
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@fastretail.com>, Tom Hayes <t.hayes@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot readiness: hosted endpoints, rate ceilings, and VPC decision inputs

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — really appreciate the clarity you and Tom brought around the checkout flow and fraud-checking use case. Quick written recap and a few asks to make sure our pilot proposal matches your expectations.

Summary of what we demoed
- Hosted API endpoints for inference (text generation + embeddings)
- Prefix/KV cache to reduce token cost for repeated contexts
- Routing/fallback behavior to smaller variants if capacity is constrained

Open questions for FastRetail to confirm
1) Target pilot QPS / tokens per minute (approx): what would peak look like during testing?
2) Data classification: can the initial pilot use Hosted API (data stays in Redwood multi-tenant environment) or do you need Private VPC/on-prem from day one? You mentioned security would prefer VPC long-term — that's fine; we can stage the pilot on Hosted if the data is allowed.
3) Success criteria and timeline: do you want a 2-week sandbox pilot or a 4-week production-congruent pilot?

Short next steps I propose
- We provision sandbox endpoints (hosted) and share endpoint + API keys — onboard in 48 hours after you confirm traffic profile.
- Fill the attached quickstart spreadsheet with expected concurrency, average request/response token counts, and peak windows. That helps us size rate ceilings correctly.
- Security: if security wants to run our questionnaire, we can get that to them and also list required artifacts (SOC2 summary, data retention policy).

Attachments: FastRetail-quickstart-checklist.xlsx (please fill the "traffic profile" tab), fastretail-network-diagram.png (for reference)

If Hosted is acceptable for the pilot, we will default to our managed endpoint rate policy and can request temporary higher ceilings for the sandbox. If you need Dedicated/VPC for legal reasons we can propose a Dedicated reserved plan with a guided rollout.

Would you be able to send the traffic profile and your preferred pilot duration by EOD Friday?

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0187

Thanks, Chloe — great demo. A few clarifications from our side (security and platform):

- Data: Our default stance is to prefer VPC for production. Security said they can sign off for a short, scoped Hosted pilot if we guarantee PII-free payloads and we run inside sandbox endpoints (no long-term retention). Is that how you handle sandbox Hosted endpoints?
- Rate questions: would you confirm what the "default" hosted rate ceilings look like (requests per minute, tokens per minute) and what the process is for a temporary bump during pilot? Also: what happens if we exceed the ceiling — graceful throttling or errors?
- Procurement: our procurement team wants a sample SOW/SoW or order form to review in parallel — can you send a template?

We can aim to have the traffic sheet back to you by Monday. Also copying Tom so he sees the next steps on procurement.

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: hosted endpoints, rate ceilings, and VPC decision inputs

Hi Alyssa / Tom — quick answers inline and a proposed pilot plan.

Sandbox Hosted behavior (short answer)
- Sandbox Hosted endpoints: yes, scoped non-persistent storage for logs and no long-term model inputs retained (we provide a data handling summary you can pass to security). We will label the environment as sandbox and apply a retention policy for debugging logs only.

Default Hosted rate ceilings (pilot-friendly) — these are the defaults we aim for; we size per-account and can temporarily increase for pilots once we have the traffic profile:
- Endpoint request ceiling: 120 requests per minute per endpoint (default)
- Token throughput guideline: ~60,000 tokens per minute for pilot sandboxes (burstable based on usage patterns)
- Bursting: short spikes are handled via our autoscaling and burst pool; if sustained above the ceiling we apply graceful 429 throttles with Retry-After headers and circuit-breaker fallbacks to a lower-cost model variant.

If you expect higher sustained throughput during the pilot, we can request an elevated ceiling for your sandbox (typically approved within 24 hours with the traffic sheet). For strict low-latency SLO and predictable throughput under high sustained load we recommend Dedicated capacity.

Procurement / SOW
- Attached: a short SoW template and the quickstart checklist (FastRetail-quickstart-checklist.xlsx). I also added a "procurement notes" tab with suggested line items for a 4-week pilot and an optional Dedicated uplift.

Proposed immediate next steps (if Hosted pilot OK)
1) You complete the traffic profile tab in the attached spreadsheet (concurrency, avg tokens per request, peak windows).
2) We provision sandbox endpoints and send keys (48–72 hours).
3) Monica (onboarding) will schedule a 60-minute prep call to walk through the keys and sample integrations.

If security wants the questionnaire, I can route it to your team today — Marissa will follow up with the SOC2 and data handling doc.

Attachments referenced: FastRetail-quickstart-checklist.xlsx, fastretail-network-diagram.png

Open items I will action now:
- Upload SoW template to DocuSign and share link (I’ll add that to this thread when ready).
- Marissa will attach SOC2 summary and short data handling one-pager.

Best,
Chloe
